## Active

### D-305 — Coral stays on the database while the other three marine models are mocked

> _2026-09-28 · demo/blong-marine · active_

meta/db/db.ts declares mock for marineFamilyModel, marineSpeciesModel and marineHabitatModel only,
and that is deliberate: the shared srv.db adapter serves those three models from marineFixture data
while marine.coral keeps its real MySQL table and its marineCoralMerge.yaml seed, so the Playwright
suite exercises the DB path and the server-side mock path in one run and a regression in either
shows up. It is also what lets the realm be inspected without a database. Anything that changes it
should keep at least one model on each path; T-148 records one consequence (the mocked lists do not
honour a browse search pin the way the DB-backed one does). The browser mock adapter is independent
of this switch — it mocks every model from the same fixture.

### D-621 — Family and species edit tests pin their own record

> _2026-10-25 · demo/blong-marine · active_

The family and species edit tests now pass `search` to `createAndEditModel` (plus
`navigatorNode: 'Gorgoniidae'` for species, whose table renders the navigator's branch), so each
spec edits the record it created instead of the first row of an unfiltered table. T-148 said the
browse search could not isolate a record on those two pages because their lists come from the mocked
models; that is no longer true — `core/blong-mock`'s `find` filters on `search`, and a local run of
either spec opened the created record once the pin was added. The reason to pin is the one F-255
records for coral: `family.play.ts`'s unpinned edit test renamed the seeded `Acroporidae` in the
shared model mock, and every later capture in the same run that showed the family tree or a species'
`familyId` label carried the test name, which is what made `species.play.ts` and `portal.play.ts`
fail in CI run 634 while the family spec itself passed.

The cost is four baselines per spec: `-open`, `-edit-dirty` and `-edit-saved` now picture the
test-created record rather than the seeded one. They were re-captured on the same machine the suite
passes on, and the untouched browse and create shots came back byte-identical, which is the check
that the capture is stable rather than merely new.

### D-741 — The marine demo mounts the same browser realms as blong-suite

> _2026-11-03 · demo/blong-marine · active_

The marine demonstration app mounts the same browser realms as `blong-suite` (`access`, `marine`,
`blong` and `kustomize`) and its manifest declares the packages those realms come from, so both
applications render one portal shell: `Access | Marine | Kustomize | Observe` under the Marine
Biology brand.

The alternative was to keep the two apps different and give each its own screenshot baselines in
`defineBlongConfig` (host-keyed `snapshotPathTemplate`). That costs a config feature plus a full
capture of the suite's copy of every marine spec on the runner, and leaves a demo whose portal is a
reduced version of the one the suites ship — while the realm's specs are shared by both apps by
design.

The cost of this choice is paid on the server side, and it is what the declaration implies: the
framework loads a realm only for a suite whose manifest declares the package (`resolveFromSuite` in
`core/blong-gogo/src/load.ts`), so declaring `blong-access` and `blong-realm` also brings their
server halves into the marine process. `blong-core` has to be declared beside them, or the access
realm's `access_user` foreign key has no `core_resource` to open and the boot dies mid-migration.
`blong-kustomize` stays declared for the browser only: its server realm is gated to the `k8s`
intent, so its page renders and answers nothing in a serving process — the same behaviour
`blong-suite` has.
